newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures continue higher on EIA crude data.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures continue higher on EIA crude data.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures continued to edge higher on Wednesday, lifted U.S. government weekly stocks data and underpinned by a North sea supply disruption, brokers said.
By 1450 GMT, front month September Brent was 13 cents higher at $18.37 a barrel, with gas oil $2.00 firmer at $165.00 a tonne, though both continued to trade in low volume.
NYMEX crude was 12 cents higher at $19.57 a barrel after
EIA data showed U.S. crude stocks fell 2.0 million barrels last week, compared with a rise of 1.42 million shown in American Petroleum Institute (API) data late on Tuesday.
"Brent's up mainly on the back of the North sea supply disruption story, and the DOE data is supportive," one broker said.
Production at the 150,000 barrels per day North Sea Nelson oilfield was shut in on Wednesday until at least Friday due a minor technical problem.
Brokers also pointed to more positive sentiment on the physical market, where physical Brent traded on Tuesday at August +10 cts.
GNI Research on Wednesday pegged strong resistance just below 18.50 per barrel, while it placed support at 18.00.
London brokers said both crude and gas oil were likely to continue to trade in narrow ranges until further news on the resumption of Iraqi crude exports transpires.
"No-one wants to trade while Iraq is up in the air. We're in a very narrow trading range. The volumes say it all, " a broker said.
A U.N. spokesman on Tuesday said the approval of Iraq's aid distribution plan, which Iraq insists on before it resumes exports, was not expected until the end of July.
